This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. A monumental 12th-century gilt-copper-alloy figure of Manjushri, cataloged as originating from Nepal, has set a new world auction record for Himalayan sculpture. It sold for HK$137.35 million (approximately US$17.5 million) at Christie's in Hong Kong, more than doubling its presale estimate after sustained bidding. The sculpture was the standout piece of the dedicated sale *"Awakening Wisdom: Masterpieces of Buddhist Art from a Private Asian Collection."* Christie's official catalogue attributes the work to 12th-century Nepal, a reminder of the enduring global prestige and masterful craftsmanship of the Kathmandu Valley's artistic heritage. International auction houses often group works like this under broad departments such as "Indian, Himalayan and Southeast Asian Art," but the catalogue itself places this masterpiece in Nepal. For the country's cultural legacy, it's a proud, record-breaking moment on the global stage. Follow @neptera.official for more updates! #NepTera #NepaliArt #Manjushri #CulturalHeritage #ChristiesAuction Source: Christie's Official Auction Catalogue: [Awakening Wisdom: Masterpieces of Buddhist Art, Lot 2007](https://www.christies.com/en/lot/lot-6610482) MartinCID & Artnet: [Christie's Hong Kong Asian Art Autumn 2026 Manjushri Record](https://www.martincid.com/art/christies-hong-kong-asian-art-autumn-2026-manjushri-record-bada-shanren/) Verification note: The sculpture is cataloged by Christie's as originating from 12th-century Nepal.
